holidays.name: National Draw a Dinosaur Day
holidays.description: Grab a marker, a crayon, or a napkin and sketch your best stegosaurus, T. rex, or made-up dino. Artistic skill is optional and scales are encouraged.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, popular with classrooms, families and dinosaur fans.
holidays.funFact: Many of the dinosaur pictures you grew up with are out of date. Scientists now think lots of dinosaurs, including some relatives of T. rex, had feathers.

holidays.name: National Croissant Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the buttery, flaky, crescent-shaped pastry. Eat one plain, stuff it with ham and cheese, or dunk it in coffee.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance that honors the beloved pastry of French bakeries and brunch tables everywhere.
holidays.funFact: The croissant is descended from the Austrian kipferl. It became the flaky pastry we know today in 20th-century France, when bakers began making it with laminated yeast dough.

holidays.name: National Inane Answering Message Day
holidays.description: Record the silliest, most pointless voicemail greeting you can think of. It's a day for goofy outgoing messages that make callers smile, or groan.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin. It dates from the answering-machine era, and is also listed as National Inane Answering Machine Day.
holidays.funFact: The holiday started in the days of tape-based answering machines. Voicemail greetings were once a small art form, and callers sometimes dialed just to hear a funny one.
